City of Chicago Black Renaissance landmark report
entities.name: Chicago Public Library
entities.notes: Parent institution of the Harsh Collection and the Harold Washington Archives & Collections. Harsh is its flagship Black research collection; HWLC Special Collections (9th floor) hold the Harold Washington papers.
entities.privacy_status: no private data; public institutional addresses only

entities.name: Vivian G. Harsh Research Collection of Afro-American History and Literature
entities.notes: Housed at the Carter G. Woodson Regional Library, Washington Heights. Described by CPL as the Midwest's largest Black history collection (institutional self-description). Currently closed for maintenance (C001).

entities.name: Abbott-Sengstacke Family Papers
entities.notes: The Chicago Defender's founding-family archive. Kept in Chicago by donor choice after national bids. ~83 boxes, ~4,000 photos, ~100 home movies. Must not be equated with the Defender's corporate archive (C066).

evidence: chipublib.org — Illinois Writers Project finding aid
entities.name: Illinois Writers Project 'Negro in Illinois' Papers
entities.notes: 1936–1942, 53 boxes, no restrictions, majority digitized. Strongest digitization example in the Harsh holdings.

evidence: Legal Talk Network podcast (Feb 2025) — Irmer interview
entities.name: DuSable Black History Museum and Education Center
entities.notes: Founded 1961 as the Ebony Museum of Negro History. Collection size DISPUTED (13,000 vs 15,000+). Archive access: by appointment (SUPPORTED, not primary).
entities.privacy_status: no private data; publicly documented addresses only

entities.name: Chicago History Museum — Abakanowicz Research Center
entities.notes: Most openly accessible major repository: free, no appointment required. Some finding aids temporarily offline (C021).

entities.name: Black Metropolis Research Consortium
entities.notes: Launched 2006 at UChicago (host). 20+ members (own video: 26). Searchable Archives Portal; 95 summer fellowships since 2008 (ca. 2019).

entities.name: Newberry Library
entities.notes: Independent research library. Black Chicago strengths: Pullman Company Records, Jack Conroy Papers, Mark J. Satter Papers, Great Migration lantern slides (1922–23). Reading rooms free with free reader card.

entities.name: University of Chicago — Hanna Holborn Gray Special Collections Research Center
entities.notes: Ida B. Wells Papers; Julius Rosenwald Papers (1905–1963, 44 linear feet, unrestricted). BMRC host; namesake context: Drake and Cayton's Black Metropolis (1945).

entities.name: Northwestern University Libraries
entities.notes: BMRC member; board representation. Collection-level Black Chicago descriptions not verified in this pilot.

entities.name: University of Illinois Chicago — Special Collections and University Archives
entities.notes: Black strengths: Chicago Urban League Records, Hyde Park Neighborhood Club Records, Maxwell Street Exhibition Photographs. Appointment-only (SUPPORTED via BMRC page; confirm against UIC's own page before reuse).

entities.name: Chicago State University — Gwendolyn Brooks Library
entities.notes: Focus: African American history, literature, politics; Chicago neighborhoods. Holds Brooks Black Writers' Conference AV, Lerone Bennett Jr. Papers, Provident Hospital Collection, and more.

entities.name: South Side Community Art Center
entities.notes: Founded 1940 (committee 1938); oldest African American art center in the U.S.; National Treasure (2017). Archives: 75 linear feet, 1938–2008, appointment-only. $15M renovation, completion anticipated 2027.

entities.name: Cook County Historic Archives and Records Office
entities.notes: Established 2020; first Manager of Archives Skyla Hearn. Currently closed to the public; remote reference only.

entities.name: Shorefront Legacy Center
entities.notes: Founded by Morris 'Dino' Robinson; ~30 years documenting Black life on Chicago's North Shore; housed in the basement of Evanston's Lula B. Sherman Church. Records underpinned Evanston's reparations research. Exact access terms UNRESOLVED.
entities.privacy_status: no private data; church basement is the archive's own stated location in NPR coverage

evidence: Rebuild Foundation collection descriptions; press coverage
entities.name: Rebuild Foundation
entities.notes: Artist-led nonprofit (501(c)(3) December 2010; founder Theaster Gates). Stony Island Arts Bank (Greater Grand Crossing): 60,000+ lantern slides, JPC books/periodicals, Frankie Knuckles vinyl, Edward J. Williams Collection. Stated research-access policy UNRESOLVED.

entities.name: Columbia College Chicago — Center for Black Music Research
entities.notes: BMRC founding-discussion participant; temporarily housed SSAC administrative archives during renovation.

entities.name: Johnson Publishing Company archive
entities.notes: Founded 1942. 4M+ images, 9,000+ recordings, ~2.25 TB digital, textual records. Sold 2019 ($30M); transferred July 28, 2022 to joint NMAAHC + Getty Research Institute ownership; physically housed at NMAAHC, Washington, DC. Getty committed $30M to processing/digitization. No longer in Chicago.

entities.name: Chicago Defender archive
entities.notes: Print ended July 10, 2019; continues online. Founding-family papers at CPL/Harsh (E-ABBOTT-SENGSTACKE). Backfiles 1909–1975 via ProQuest. Obsidian Collection digitizes Black newspaper archives incl. the Defender. Custodianship of the paper's own business/operational archives after 2019: UNRESOLVED.

entities.name: Obsidian Collection Archives
entities.notes: Nonprofit (executive director Angela Ford) digitizing Black newspaper archives including the Chicago Defender.

entities.name: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture
entities.notes: Joint owner and physical custodian of the JPC archive (with the Getty Research Institute). Appears only as a custodial endpoint, not an inventoried Chicago collection.

entities.name: Getty Research Institute
entities.notes: Joint owner of the JPC archive with NMAAHC; committed $30M to processing/digitization.

entities.name: Vivian G. Harsh
entities.notes: CPL's first African American branch manager (January 18, 1932); founded the Special Negro Collection. Public historical figure; deceased 1960.

entities.name: Margaret Taylor-Burroughs; Charles Burroughs
entities.notes: Co-founded the Ebony Museum of Negro History (1961), seed of the DuSable. Public historical figures.

entities.name: Theaster Gates
entities.notes: Artist; founder of Rebuild Foundation (2010). Living public figure; institutional role only.

entities.name: Morris 'Dino' Robinson; Laurice Bell
entities.notes: Robinson founded Shorefront Legacy Center; Bell runs its archive. Public institutional roles.

entities.name: Skyla S. Hearn
entities.notes: First Manager of Archives, Cook County Historic Archives and Records Office (2020). Public institutional role.

entities.name: JPC archive transfer (July 28, 2022)
entities.notes: Formal transfer of sole ownership of the historic Ebony and Jet archive to joint NMAAHC + Getty Research Institute ownership; physical housing at NMAAHC, Washington, DC. Confirmed displacement from Chicago.

entities.name: JPC bankruptcy auction (2019)
entities.notes: $30 million purchase by the Ford, Getty Trust, MacArthur, and Mellon foundations.

entities.name: Harsh Collection maintenance closure (2026)
entities.notes: Temporarily unavailable for research; CPL 'targeting November for reopening'; researcher wait list; remote reference continues.

entities.name: Chicago Defender ends print (July 10, 2019)
entities.notes: Continues online.
